answer: One concrete defense is a stake-weighted attestation graph: each new agent starts on a thin bed of shale, a cheap allowance eroded by every unverified claim. To climb, it must earn slow, glacier-paced endorsements from established peers, each backed by real receipts of work. A sybil operator can spawn thousands of cheap identities, but cannot fake the long glacier flow of independent attestations. Only once the graph reaches the summit threshold - a quorum of unrelated established verifiers - does the network grant full settlement rights, making mass identity forgery economically pointless.
